I'll search for what's on record about the Suzuki step.Good—I have several Suzuki notes. Let me expand the central ones to get the full detail.Excellent. Now let me expand the recent ELN runs and the playbooks to fill in the picture.Perfect. Here is what we know about the Suzuki step, structured into four buckets:

---

## **I. Starting Materials and Sources**

**Aryl halides:**
- [[compound-4-bromoanisole]] (COc1ccc(Br)cc1) — electron-rich bromide, deliberately unfavourable substrate for oxidative addition [[rxn-suzuki-biaryl]] (confidence 0.85)
- Electron-rich chlorides do not couple under the standard conditions (80 °C, 12 h) — this is the scope boundary [[campaign-biaryl-scope]] (confidence 0.8)

**Boronic acids:**
- [[compound-phenylboronic-acid]] (OB(O)c1ccccc1) — phenylboronic acid [[rxn-suzuki-biaryl]]

**Bases:**
- K₂CO₃ (2.0 equiv) — preferred base in optimized conditions [[opt-suzuki-conditions]] (confidence 0.85)

**Solvents:**
- THF/water 4:1 — organic-aqueous two-phase system [[rxn-suzuki-biaryl]]
- 1,4-dioxane/water 4:1 — used in recent bench runs [[reaction-uspto-suzuki-biphenyl-1]] (confidence null; ELN extracted)

---

## **II. Reaction Conditions**

**Temperature and time:**
- Optimized: 80 °C, 12 h — gives 76% isolated yield [[opt-suzuki-conditions]], [[rxn-suzuki-biaryl]]
- Recent runs at 82 °C, 4 h — gives 89.5–92.5% isolated yield (higher temperature + shorter time, both with P(tBu)₃) [[reaction-uspto-suzuki-biphenyl-1]], [[reaction-uspto-suzuki-biphenyl-2]]

**Catalyst and ligand:**
- Pd(OAc)₂ (1.5 mol%) with no specified ligand — 76% isolated [[rxn-suzuki-biaryl]] (confidence 0.85)
- Pd(0) precursor with P(tBu)₃ ligand — 89–92% isolated in 4 h at 82 °C [[reaction-uspto-suzuki-biphenyl-1]], [[reaction-uspto-suzuki-biphenyl-2]] (ELN source)

**Degassing:**
- Essential: three freeze-pump-thaw cycles OR 20 min sparge per 100 mL solvent
- Two minutes of sparging is insufficient and causes bimodal yield (70%+ or <20%)
- Mechanism: Pd(0) is oxidized by dissolved O₂ to catalytically dead black precipitate [[playbook-degassing]] (confidence 0.85)

---

## **III. Known Failure Modes**

**Protodeboronation (boronic acid self-decomposition):**
- At 100 °C in THF/water, LCAP conversion rises to 79% but isolated yield drops to 68% [[opt-suzuki-conditions]], [[failure-aqueous-protodeboronation]]
- The boronic acid protodeboronates to benzene faster than it transmetalates at elevated temperature [[failure-aqueous-protodeboronation]] (confidence 0.8)
- This failure was observed three times before recognized because assay (LCAP) looked better each time — a cautionary note on readout choice [[failure-aqueous-protodeboronation]]

**Catalyst deactivation by oxygen:**
- Bimodal yield distribution (high or low, rarely intermediate) signals incomplete degassing [[playbook-degassing]]

**Aryl halide scope:**
- Electron-rich aryl chlorides do not couple at 80 °C, 12 h under standard conditions [[campaign-biaryl-scope]] (confidence 0.8)

---

## **IV. Controls and Process Knowledge**

**Assay vs. isolated yield gap:**
- The gap between LCAP conversion and isolated yield is a key finding; optimizing on the wrong readout (assay alone) would have selected the hotter, worse condition [[opt-suzuki-conditions]] (confidence 0.85)

**Ligand strategy before temperature:**
- For electron-rich aryl halides, oxidative addition is the rate-limiting step and responds far more strongly to ligand steric bulk than to temperature [[playbook-pd-cross-coupling-scope]] (confidence 0.8)
- Recommended escalation order: bulkier biaryl phosphine → higher L:Pd ratio → harder degassing → *only then* more heat [[playbook-pd-cross-coupling-scope]]

**Recent bench outcomes:**
- [[reaction-uspto-suzuki-biphenyl-1]]: 89.5% isolated, 98.2% purity, impurities include 1.4% des-methoxy biphenyl and 0.3% unreacted bromide (J. Alvarez, 2024-01-08)
- [[reaction-uspto-suzuki-biphenyl-2]]: 92.5% isolated, 97.8% purity (M. Chen, 2024, similar conditions)

---

**Key transferable insight:** The boundary of this system is electron-rich *bromides* at 80 °C; chlorides require different conditions. Temperature can mask protodeboronation loss. Degassing is binary — either adequate or the catalyst is dead.
